title: Fixed-scalar finite projection/exchange coordinates
statement: For a finite commutative ring A and a scheme X, put Dcat(A,X)=D(Sh(X_proet,Mod(A))). Let pull(A,f)=Lf*, push(A,f)=Rf*, and tensor be the published derived tensor; tensorMap(a,b) is tensor(a,1) followed by tensor(1,b). Let mu be the canonical derived pullback/tensor isomorphism and theta:Fprime G -> H F the canonical comparison of a commutative square. Let pi be the counit-defined right-derived projection and exchange the mate of theta, as in [def-exchange-projection]. properFirst is G(pi); exchange; Sprime(mu_H; tensor(1,theta.inv)), exchangeFirst is mu_G; tensor(exchange,1); pi_prime, and commonTranspose is Fprime(mu_G); mu_Fprime; tensor(theta,1); tensor(H(counit),1). For an open immersion j, ext is derived extension by zero, gamma is its tensor projection isomorphism, beta:H ext_j -> ext_jprime A is the canonical open base-change isomorphism, and openUnitInv is the inverse open adjunction unit. openFirst and openSecond are respectively H(gamma); beta; ext_jprime(mu_A; tensor(1,theta.inv)) and mu_H; tensor(beta,1); gamma_prime. openSource is the canonical pullback/tensor identification followed by the open unit inverses. For a compactification c=pj of f, pf and ex are the supplied compactification projection and exchange of [def-exchange-projection]; target is mu_A followed by tensor(1,theta.inv); diamondLeft is G(pf_c); ex_c; S_prime(target), and diamondRight is mu_G; tensor(ex_c,1); pf_cprime. identitySupport is the direct-image identity comparison followed by the extension identity comparison. baseRefinement pulls a refinement back along a cartesian square; rho is the specified compact-support refinement comparison of [def-fix-six-functor-datum], conjugated by the supplied etale-origin object isomorphism. RefinementLaw says both diamond words intertwine rho. SquareLaw conjoins diamond equality, the two open essential-image and restriction claims, the two common-transpose claims, and RefinementLaw. IdentityLaw says the identity-compactification projection becomes the identity after identitySupport and pullback identity comparisons. finiteBC and finiteCTF are the given coefficient-stage bounded-constructible and finite-Tor predicates. These are explicit composites, with no new choices.
